title: Reliability Baseline & Conditional Throttle Framework
creator: Aisha Patel
description: This initiative creates a reproducible baseline for key reliability SLIs across hosted and dedicated deployments, and implements a Conditional Throttle Framework (CTF) that automatically applies graduated traffic throttles when error-budget burn or SLI degradation cross configurable thresholds. The goal is to reduce large-scale incidents by proactively degrading non-critical paths and protecting core latency/availability for paying customers. Work includes baseline telemetry, simulation harness, throttle policy engine, console UX for policy configuration, and a runbook for escalation and rollback.
acceptance_criteria: Baseline SLI measurement: 14-day rolling SLI baseline computed for 95th token-latency, success-rate, and model-fallback frequency for hosted and dedicated clusters
CTF policy engine can enforce 3 throttle levels (soft, moderate, hard) based on SLI thresholds and error-budget burn rate
Console UX: policy editor & realtime preview of throttle impact with simulated load; permissions bound to tenant admin roles
Automated canary: rollout gating uses CTF outputs to block full rollouts when projected error-budget depletion within 72 hours
Runbook: documented manual override, post-incident analysis template, and SRE/PM notification wire-up
tasks: Instrument: add SLI tags and 14-day window aggregations to metrics pipeline (ENG-41012)
Simulate: build a synthetic load harness and smoke tests to model throttle outcomes
Policy engine: implement thresholding service and durable policy store
Console: add policy editor UI and preview simulator (design mock linked)
Runbook & Alerts: create playbook and alert mappings to PagerDuty escalation paths

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Overly aggressive throttling may violate SLAs for paying customers. Mitigation: conservative default thresholds, manual override, and per-tenant opt-out for Dedicated customers.
Risk: Telemetry lag could cause late or incorrect throttle decisions. Mitigation: use short-window predictions with fallback to safe defaults and require min-data quorum before escalations.
Risk: Complexity in console UX leads to misconfiguration. Mitigation: provide presets, validation, and 'dry-run' preview for each policy change.
notes: Non-goal: This initiative will not change model-serving kernels or quantization levels; focus is on traffic shaping and SLI-based protection.
Follow-up: If CTF reduces incidents as expected, propose Q2 project to integrate CTF with cost-optimization signals (batching/quantization recommendations).
Operational metric to track post-launch: % of incidents where CTF reduced blast radius and time-to-recovery
